statements.statement: Two I2C devices on the same bus can have the same address without causing any issues.
statements.explanation: No two devices on the same I2C bus can have the same address. If they did, both would try to respond simultaneously, causing communication errors.

statements.statement: All devices on an I2C bus share the same two wires (SDA and SCL).
statements.explanation: Every device on an I2C bus shares the same SDA and SCL wires and responds only when it hears its own unique address.

statements.statement: Some I2C modules let you change their address with a solder jumper or configuration pin.
statements.explanation: Some modules allow address changes via a solder jumper or configuration pin, specifically so you can use two of the same sensor on one bus.
